verifications.claim: The February 2026 Producer Price Index (PPI) report showed a 0.7% rise in wholesale prices.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The ⁠Producer Price Index for final demand surged 0.7% last month" (R1); "PPI for final demand advances 0.7% in February" (R3); "The U.S. Producer Price Index for February rose 0.7%" (R5); "The Producer Price Index for final demand increased 0.7 percent in February" (R7); "The producer price index... increased a seasonally adjusted 0.7%" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm 0.7% monthly rise in PPI/final demand for February 2026; 'wholesale prices' is synonymous with PPI.

verifications.claim: The 12-month PPI hit 3.4% according to the February 2026 PPI report.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In the 12 months through February, the PPI increased 3.4%" (R1); "The index for final demand rose 3.4 percent for the 12 months ended in February" (R3); "the index for final demand rose 3.4 percent for the 12 months ended in February" (R7); "On a 12-month basis, headline PPI inflation was at 3.4%" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match across BLS and news sources for 12-month PPI at 3.4% through February 2026.

verifications.claim: The 12-month PPI of 3.4% was the highest since February 2025.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the fastest rate of growth in a year" (R1, implying since Feb 2025); Table A shows Feb 2025: 3.4%, then lower until Feb 2026: 3.4% (R7); "headline PPI inflation was at 3.4%, the most since February 2025" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm 3.4% matches or is the highest since Feb 2025 (tied per table, explicitly stated in R9).

verifications.claim: PPI for final demand rose 0.7% according to the February 2026 PPI report.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The ⁠Producer Price Index for final demand surged 0.7%" (R1); "PPI for final demand advances 0.7% in February" (R3); "PPI for February rose 0.7%" (R5); "The Producer Price Index for final demand increased 0.7 percent in February" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing and value confirmed in primary BLS and reporting sources.

verifications.claim: The forecast for the PPI monthly gain was 0.3%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a gain of 0.3%" (R1); "0.7% versus just 0.3% expected" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements on economist forecasts for February monthly PPI.

verifications.claim: The 12-month PPI rise in January was 2.9%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "followed a 2.9% advance in January" (R1); Table A: Jan 2026 2.9% (R7)

verifications.claim: Core PPI rose 0.5% for the month.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the core PPI rose 0.5% versus 0.3% expected" (R5); "Excluding volatile food and energy costs, the so-called core PPI increased 0.5%" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Direct reports of core PPI monthly rise of 0.5% in February; R7 has similar 'less foods, energy, trade' at 0.5%.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact annual core PPI figure from reliable source.

verifications.claim: Core PPI excludes food and energy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Core PPI... excludes volatile food and energy prices" (implied in R2 also, but R6 defines PPI and notes core excludes); standard definition confirmed.
verifications.reasoning: Wikipedia and common usage directly state core PPI definition excludes food and energy.

verifications.claim: The index for final demand goods jumped 1.1%.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Producer goods prices soared 1.1%" (R1); "goods increase 1.1%" (R3); "Prices for final demand goods increased 1.1 percent" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match for final demand goods index.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The 0.5% rise in services" (R1); "services rise 0.5%" (R3); "final demand services rose 0.5 percent" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for services increase in final demand PPI.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "48.9% jump in the cost of fresh and dry vegetables" (R1); "48.9-percent jump in prices for fresh and dry vegetables" (R7)

verifications.claim: The PPI measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers for their output.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "a producer price index (PPI) is a price index that measures the average changes in prices received by domestic producers for their output" (R6); "measures the average change over time in prices received (price changes) by producers for domestically produced goods" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Precise definition from Wikipedia and BLS.

verifications.claim: The headline PPI figure includes food and energy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Headline vs core distinction; core "excludes volatile food and energy costs" (R9); PPI full measure includes all, core excludes (R6, R7)
verifications.reasoning: Standard terminology: headline PPI is total, includes food/energy; core excludes.

verifications.claim: The next PPI report is scheduled to be released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics on April 15, 2026.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "The Producer Price Index for March 2026 is scheduled to be released on Tuesday, April 14, 2026"
verifications.reasoning: BLS specifies April 14, 2026, not 15; direct contradiction on date.
